title: The Bosphorus Brief — Saturday, 26 September 2026
overview: A quieter weekend news day dominated by football (Turkey's 0-1 loss to France) sits alongside more consequential developments for residents: a lira-relevant dip in central bank reserves, tightening visa rules in Montenegro, and steady residency enforcement at home. Regional tensions around Iran and the Pakistan-Afghanistan border continue, though neither directly touches daily life in Türkiye.

sections.heading: Money: Reserves Slip, Inflation Outlook Unchanged
sections.body: Turkey's central bank reserves fell by $4.3 billion amid what opposition-leaning Turkish Minute describes as fund market turmoil. Separately, the OECD projects Turkish inflation will stay elevated for longer than earlier hoped. For residents budgeting in lira, today's rates are USD/TRY 48.89, EUR/TRY 55.65, and GBP/TRY 64.64 — worth checking before any large transfers or rent renewals this week. The central bank also revoked the operating license of e-money firm Papel Elektronik Para; anyone using that service for transfers or bill payments should confirm alternative arrangements promptly.

sections.heading: Residency and Visas: Enforcement and New Restrictions
sections.body: Nationwide inspections led to the arrest of six people found without valid ikamet, a reminder that spot checks continue and permits should be kept current and on hand. In Cyprus, one case highlighted a person left 1,390 days without residence permission — a stark example of how backlogs can drag on; those with pending or lapsed applications should follow up with authorities rather than let cases go quiet. Abroad, Montenegro is moving to end visa-free travel for Turkish, Russian, and Belarusian passport holders, which would affect Turkish citizens' travel plans there once implemented. Separately, North Macedonia's citizenship applications are reportedly taking years to process — useful context for anyone pursuing dual citizenship in the region.

sections.heading: Rights Watch: A Deportation Concern Flagged
sections.body: Hana Human Rights Organization has warned of an imminent deportation threat facing one of its members in Turkey; details remain limited, but it's the kind of case we'll continue to track as more information becomes available. Elsewhere, Germany is deporting a Turkish man involved in a fatal speed-racing case, illustrating how criminal proceedings abroad can intersect with residency status for Turkish nationals in Europe.

sections.heading: Safety and Travel Notes
sections.body: No new earthquakes above M4 have struck Türkiye since the M5.3 near Hilvan on September 24; seismic activity remains within the normal range for the region. US travel advisories are unchanged: Türkiye remains Level 2. Regionally, tensions continue over Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and a Pakistan-Afghanistan border clash with disputed casualty figures — worth monitoring if your travel or work touches those areas, though there's no indication of spillover into Türkiye itself.

closing: Stay dry, keep your paperwork handy, and enjoy the weekend — çay's on us.
